name: Lazy Peons
summary: Foreman Thazz'ril sends new Horde recruits across the Valley of Trials to wake sleeping peons. Their work keeps lumber moving to Durotar's settlements.

sections.title: Slacking in the Sun
sections.body: Durotar's new homes need timber, stone, and hard labor. Peons, orcs with little skill in battle, carry much of that burden and keep the Horde supplied with workers. In the Valley of Trials, the heat and grueling work leave Foreman Thazz'ril's crews seeking shade beneath trees for unauthorized naps.

sections.title: A Swift Wake-Up Call
sections.body: Foreman Thazz'ril gives new Horde recruits his blackjack and sends them across the valley to wake the sleeping workers. The startled peons return to chopping wood, keeping lumber flowing for Durotar's survival.

faq.q: Why are the peons falling asleep?
faq.answer: Gathering heavy lumber under Durotar's punishing sun is exhausting work. Peons slip beneath large trees to rest when no supervisor is nearby.
Foreman Thazz'ril oversees the labor crews in the Valley of Trials. They harvest lumber and supplies for the Horde's new construction.
The Foreman's Blackjack is a heavy leather sap that Thazz'ril uses to discipline slacking workers. A blow to the head wakes a sleeping peon without causing permanent injury.

faq.q: What role do peons have in the Horde?
faq.answer: Peons form the laboring class of orcish society. Though physically stout, they are considered unfit for war and work instead as builders, miners, and woodcutters for Horde settlements and its war machine.

faq.q: Where do I find the sleeping peons?
faq.answer: You can find sleeping peons throughout the Valley of Trials, north and south of the Den. Look beneath the wide tree canopies where workers seek shade.

faq.q: What happens after the peons are awakened?
faq.answer: After you return the blackjack to Foreman Thazz'ril, he sends you to recover his lost mining pick from a nearby cave.

angles.text: As a young orc coming of age, you learn the harsh realities and practical discipline of building a nation from the wilderness by disciplining your kin's workers.
As a Darkspear troll training alongside your allies, you see the brute strength and managerial exasperation behind orcish construction.
As a member of the Horde, you know every Durotar outpost depends on peon-harvested timber, so keeping the workers on the job matters to all.
